deployment: Railway (Railpack: npm run build then npm start)
@sveltejs/adapter-node (build/ served by `node build` on Railway PORT)

backend: Remult (entities, REST API, validation) via remult/remult-sveltekit

constraints: No server routes exist (src/routes/api/*/+server.ts absent), so there is no backend layer of any kind.
No database, ORM, or persistence — all state is in-memory or localStorage.
CHART_IMG_API_KEY and SUPADATA_API_KEY are inlined into the client bundle by Vite define; the Gemini key is user-supplied at runtime via ApiKeyModal.

features.name: All-Trades Table
features.summary: Sortable, filterable table of every logged trade, built with TanStack Table v9.
features.userStory: As a user, I want one table of every trade any YouTuber mentioned, with channel, asset, direction, prices and eventual P/L, so I can scan performance at a glance.

rationale: Decisive: headless-table's core input is a Svelte store (published types: `data: ReadOrWritable<Item[]>`), and `Subscribe` + `let:` slot props are the documented render path. Svelte 5 deprecates slots, and bridging `$props()` into a store reintroduces the $state-mirror pattern removed from +page.svelte in 7976487. TanStack v9 takes a plain array through a getter and stays rune-reactive off table.getRowModel().

Supporting: shadcn-svelte's own Data Table is built on TanStack Table v9, so the shadcn argument favours TanStack — though shadcn-svelte is not installed here and needs Tailwind 4 (repo is on Tailwind 3), making it a future factor rather than a live one.

NOT a factor — maintenance. @humanspeak/svelte-headless-table is actively maintained: v6.2.0, repo pushed 2026-09-02, feature commits through Aug 2026, peerDeps svelte ^5.30.0 (Svelte 5 only). The dead package is the unscoped `svelte-headless-table` (0.18.3, Oct 2024) — a different project.

WITHDRAWN — an earlier draft cited headless-table's shadcn guide using Bits UI's removed `asChild let:builder`. That is documentation staleness, not a library defect; headless-table does not depend on Bits UI at all.
Tradeoff accepted: headless-table ships first-party addVirtualScroll (actively improved) and addDataExport; TanStack needs @tanstack/virtual plus hand-rolled CSV.
